title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 10

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Which tools will be demonstrated?
tasks.audioText: Students in the metrology class will compare measuring tools on Monday at nine. The session will begin with a demonstration of a steel rule, vernier calliper and micrometer. Students should bring their measurement notebooks. The instructor will explain that the appropriate tool depends on the feature being measured and the required accuracy.
options: A steel rule, vernier calliper and micrometer

tasks.audioText: Students in the metrology class will compare measuring tools on Monday at nine. The session will begin with a demonstration of a steel rule, vernier calliper and micrometer. Students should bring their measurement notebooks. The instructor will explain that the appropriate tool depends on the feature being measured and the required accuracy.

tasks.prompt: A trainee needed to measure the outside diameter of a small cylindrical part. The steel rule was not suitable because its scale did not provide the required level of detail. The trainee selected a vernier calliper and checked that the instrument was clean and in good condition. The measured value was recorded with the correct unit and the tool used was named in the inspection note. Reading 1. Why was the steel rule unsuitable?
options: Its scale did not provide the required level of detail

tasks.prompt: What did the trainee record in the inspection note?
options: The measured value, correct unit and tool used

tasks.prompt: A vernier calliper ___ to measure the outside diameter.
Choose TWO factors to consider when selecting a measuring tool.
options: The colour of the tool case

tasks.prompt: The degree of closeness between a measurement and the true value is measurement ___.
You are not sure which instrument is suitable. What should you ask?
options: I will use the first tool I find.
Which instrument is appropriate for this feature and required accuracy?
I will estimate the measurement by eye.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of measurement tools in a logical order.
options: Identify the feature to be measured
Record the value with its unit and tool
correctOrder: Identify the feature to be measured
Record the value with its unit and tool

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to choose a measuring tool for a component. Include the feature, required accuracy and recording of results.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
